official.deadline_central_display: November 1, 2026 (Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match); February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision); March 1, 2027 (Transfer)
official.deadline_note: The same deadlines apply to the CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC; late applications are accepted but the aid decision is delayed.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 school year (instructions on the official page are for 2027-2028)
official.status_note: The financial aid application process for the 2027-2028 school year is published and open on the official site.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: "For families with incomes up to $200,000, financial aid will cover at least the full cost of tuition" and, for families with annual incomes below $100,000, "the expected parent contribution is zero."
benefits: Need-blind admissions: financial need and the aid application never affect the chance of admission
100% of demonstrated financial need met with an individualized package of scholarship funds, student employment and outside awards

Families with annual incomes below $100,000 pay nothing: aid covers all billed expenses plus a $2,000 start-up grant (first year), health insurance if needed, travel costs between campus and home, winter gear and event fees, and a $2,000 launch grant (junior year)
Families with incomes up to $200,000: financial aid covers at least the full cost of tuition
Loans are never required to attend Harvard
eligibility: All applicants regardless of citizenship; international students are eligible for exactly the same amount of aid as U.S. students
Submit a CSS Profile and an IDOC packet; U.S. citizens and permanent residents also submit the FAFSA
Apply by the deadline for your admission round, following the instructions for the 2027-2028 school year
requirements: File the online 2027-2028 CSS Profile via the College Board including Harvard as a recipient (code 3434)
File the 2027-2028 FAFSA (Harvard code E00468) - only U.S. citizens, permanent residents and other eligible non-citizens file it
Submit parents' 2025 income tax documents for both parents through College Board IDOC, including all pages and schedules
Submit the student's 2025 income tax document, or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus W-2 forms if applicable
Translate any non-English documents into English (unofficial, self-written translations are acceptable)
documents: CSS Profile (College Board) with Harvard code 3434
IDOC packet: parents' 2025 income tax document for both parents (in the U.S. usually the signed 1040 with all schedules and W-2s) and the student's 2025 income tax document
Tax Non-Filer Statement plus wage statement, salary certificate or employer letter for parents or students who do not file
Business/Farm Supplement and 2025 business tax return (1065, 1120 S or 1120 with K-1 statements) for each business or farm interest
Full trust tax return plus a letter explaining the trust or estate's contents, value and accessibility, for beneficiaries
selection_criteria: Aid is need-based only - there are no merit-based awards at Harvard College
Need is determined from family income, assets, size and unusual expenses; home equity and retirement assets are typically not considered
Late applications are accepted; a late application pushes back the aid decision but does not affect eligibility for aid
coverage: Billed costs: tuition, fees, housing and food (2026-2027 subtotal $91,634)
Estimated allowances for personal expenses ($2,500), books ($1,000) and transportation ($0-$5,000); total cost of attendance $95,134-$100,134 for 2026-2027

For families with income up to $100,000: travel costs between campus and home, health insurance if needed, winter gear, event fees and other activities, plus the $2,000 start-up and $2,000 launch grants
Health insurance is required at a cost of $4,954 (2026-27) unless the student is covered under a family health plan
application_method: File the online 2027-2028 CSS Profile via the College Board with Harvard code 3434
File the 2027-2028 FAFSA with Harvard code E00468 if you are a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or other eligible non-citizen
Upload tax and other documents through College Board IDOC once the CSS Profile is complete
Track submissions through your College Board account; aid decisions come mid-December (Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge) or around April 1 (Regular Decision)
official.application_route: CSS Profile plus IDOC for everyone, FAFSA for U.S. citizens and permanent residents, submitted alongside the admission application by your round's deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction - all applicants, including international students, follow the same aid process
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are eligible for the same amount of aid as U.S. students
official.duration: Four years; aid is reviewed annually and re-applied for each year based on need
official.description: Harvard College is need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for every admitted student regardless of citizenship, building individual packages of scholarship funds, student employment and outside awards and never requiring loans.

verification.notes: Need-blind admission, 100% need-met commitment, 2026-2027 cost of attendance, income thresholds and the Nov 1 / Feb 1 / Mar 1 deadlines were read directly from college.harvard.edu pages on 2026-10-10. No award amount is published because aid is calculated per family. fully_funded is not asserted: Harvard expects every student to cover about $3,500 of personal expenses through work-study.

applicant_utility.summary: Harvard is need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated need for everyone admitted, international students included, so the aid application cannot hurt your admission chances. File the CSS Profile plus IDOC - and the FAFSA if you are a U.S. citizen - by your round's deadline: November 1 for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match, February 1 for Regular Decision, March 1 for Transfer. Families earning under $100,000 with typical assets pay nothing, but every student is still expected to cover about $3,500 of personal expenses through work-study.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Admitted students of any nationality whose families cannot cover the full cost of attendance and can document income and assets thoroughly.
application_readiness_checklist: File taxes early - IDOC needs the actual 2025 return as filed, not drafts or estimates
Gather both parents' documents; separated or divorced parents each complete their own CSS Profile
Double-check the SSN and use your full legal name on every submission - nicknames break matching
Compare IDOC's document list against Harvard's own list; IDOC shows only the common basics
International families: translate foreign tax documents yourself; official translation is not required
common_rejection_risks: Sending tax returns with missing pages or schedules - a documented common mistake
Emailing documents to the office instead of uploading through IDOC
Applying late and expecting an on-time aid decision
Non-filing parents submitting nothing - a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus wage or employer documentation is required
International students filing the FAFSA, which they do not need
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: About $3,500 per year in personal expenses is expected from the student via work-study, plus any costs beyond the published allowances.
document_audit: Every page and schedule of the federal or national return must be included (Schedule 1, A, B and so on); state returns are not needed
Trust or estate beneficiaries need the full trust return plus an explanatory letter on contents, value and accessibility
Canadian families must submit the T-1 General (the corporate return is the T-2)
Business-owning parents need one Business/Farm Supplement and the full business return per entity
alerts: IDOC cannot be opened until the CSS Profile is submitted - sequence the two steps
If parents file for a tax extension, submit documents when available; lateness delays the decision, not eligibility
Aid is re-determined each year - keep income documentation current
Health insurance costs $4,954 in 2026-27 unless waived under a family plan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: CSS Profile, FAFSA (where applicable) and IDOC documents are submitted online alongside the admission application; decisions arrive mid-December for early rounds and around April 1 for Regular Decision.
